```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4,
                      eval = nzchar(Sys.getenv("FINNMODELFIA_RUN_VIGNETTE")))
```

`FINNmodelFIA` ships two fitted [FINN](https://github.com/FINNverse/FINN) forest
models calibrated to the US Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) network:

| variant | region | species | time step | climate inputs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `oregon` | Oregon | 27 + other | 10 years | `temp` (mean annual temperature, C), `prec` (annual precipitation, mm), WorldClim normals |
| `conus` | conterminous US | 20 | 1 year | `tavg_c`, `prec_mm` (yearly), `cwd_z` (growing-season water-deficit anomaly of the year) |

The model card with data, validation and limitations is in the
[FINN-zoo](https://finnverse.github.io/FINN-zoo/models.html). Both variants were fitted
with FINN 0.2.0 (commit 0848b60) with `weights = "auto"` and `weight_scale = "auto"`
(every loss term divided by its intercept-only baseline).

The chunks are not evaluated when the package is built (set the environment variable
`FINNMODELFIA_RUN_VIGNETTE=1` to run them): loading a model downloads the released
parameters once and needs a torch backend.

## Load a model

`load_model()` downloads the parameter list of the release this package version belongs
to (cached afterwards), checks its sha256 and rebuilds the model with the installed FINN.

```{r load}
library(FINNmodelFIA)
library(FINN)
library(data.table)

model_info()$conus[c("tag", "finn_commit", "patches", "patch_size", "step_years")]
species_table("conus")
m <- load_model("conus")
```

## Simulate example sites

Six holdout plots per variant ship with the package: the climate they saw and their
first inventory. The environment table has one row per site and simulated year with the
covariates in natural units; the initial trees become FINN cohorts with
`makeInitCohorts()`.

```{r example-sites}
ext <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "FINNmodelFIA")
env  <- fread(ext("conus_example_env.csv"))     # siteID, year, tavg_c, prec_mm, cwd_z
init <- fread(ext("conus_example_init.csv"))    # siteID, patchID, species, dbh, trees
head(env)
init_cohort <- makeInitCohorts(init, Nspecies = nrow(species_table("conus")))

sim <- simulate_model(env, init_cohort = init_cohort, variant = "conus")
out <- as.data.table(sim$long$site)
out[variable == "ba", .(ba_ha = sum(value) / model_info()$conus$patch_size), by = .(siteID, year)][order(siteID, year)][1:10]
```

`simulate_model()` is `FINN::simulateForest()` with the patch layout of the fit
(4 patches of 0.01681 ha, the four FIA subplots); `ba` and `trees` come back per patch,
so divide by `patch_size` for per-hectare values.

## Your own sites

For new sites build the same two tables: an environment table with `siteID`, `year`
(1..T) and the variant's covariates (see `read.csv(system.file("model",
"covariates.csv", package = "FINNmodelFIA"))` for units and how to derive them), and
either an initial tree list (`siteID`, `patchID` 1..4, `species` from
`species_table()`, `dbh` in cm, `trees`) or `init_cohort = NULL` for bare ground.

## Succession from bare ground

```{r bare-ground}
eq_env <- data.table(siteID = 1L, year = 1:300, tavg_c = 8, prec_mm = 900, cwd_z = 0)
sim_bg <- simulate_model(eq_env, init_cohort = NULL, variant = "conus", patches = 15L)
bg <- as.data.table(sim_bg$long$site)[variable == "ba"]
bg <- merge(bg, species_table("conus"), by = "species")
bg[, ba_ha := value / model_info()$conus$patch_size]
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(bg[ba_ha > 0.01], aes(as.integer(as.character(year)), ba_ha, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() + labs(x = "year since bare ground", y = "basal area (m2/ha)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The Oregon variant works the same way with `variant = "oregon"`; its `year` counts
10-year steps and its covariates are `temp` and `prec`.
